strengths: The paper tackles an important problem: integrating image/text understanding, 3D captioning, and high-resolution 3D generation within one MLLM. The proposed separation between sequential TokenAR modeling and parallel BlockAR modeling is intuitive and potentially useful.

The reported generation results are promising. On the stated benchmark, CG-MLLM improves over the compared MLLM-based methods in p-FID (12.55 versus 13.11 and 30.07), p-KID (0.27 versus 0.29 and 1.00), visual-quality metrics, and user preference.

The ablations provide some evidence that the Hunyuan3D-2.1 VAE, MoT architecture, larger Qwen3-VL backbone, and increased 3D-token budget each improve generation quality. The inference and memory measurements also suggest that 4096-token generation is practically feasible.
The qualitative results generally show coherent geometry and reasonable agreement with conditioning images or captions. The paper is visually clear and includes both common and rare failure examples.

The authors appropriately acknowledge that the system does not outperform all specialized non-MLLM generators, that caption data limit 3D understanding, and that watertight preprocessing and the restricted token budget reduce geometric precision.
weaknesses: The core method is substantially underspecified. The manuscript does not formally define BlockAR generation, block construction and ordering, the shared causal-parallel attention operation, cross-transformer information flow, noise/time conditioning, parameter sharing, or the complete multitask loss. The generic rectified-flow background equations do not specify the actual proposed model, making independent reproduction difficult.

Essential experimental details are missing: training-set sizes and mixture proportions, confirmation that all Toys4K test assets and near-duplicates are excluded from every training source, number of optimization steps per stage, batch composition, loss weights, learning-rate schedule, model parameter counts, and random seeds. There is also no code or artifact availability statement.

The quantitative comparison cannot be adequately audited. The test-set size, rendering protocol, number of views, metric implementations and scaling, baseline checkpoints, sampling settings, and whether every baseline was rerun on identical inputs are not reported. No confidence intervals or repeated-run variability are provided, despite several small differences such as p-KID 0.27 versus 0.29.

The user study is not reproducible or statistically interpretable: '100 questionnaires' and roughly 2,400 data points do not establish the number or recruitment of participants, rating scale, prompts, randomization, blinding, per-method comparison counts, aggregation procedure, or uncertainty/significance. Consequently, the claimed preference advantage over TRELLIS (3.32 versus 3.28) is not convincing.

The claim that learning 3D generation transfers back to perception is not causally supported. The comparison with the Qwen3-VL-2B base model lacks a matched control trained on the same captioning and image data without the 3D-generation objective. Improvements could therefore come from additional supervision or fine-tuning rather than generation itself. Comparisons between image-input and 3D-latent-input captioners are also not directly equivalent.

The claimed threefold BlockAR speedup over token-level processing is not demonstrated by the reported tables, which only vary BlockAR token length. Likewise, the text says that standard DiT versus LLM-style BlockAR was analyzed in Section 4.3, but that section instead studies AdaLN. Several ablations change multiple factors or model capacity, so they do not isolate the distinctive architectural choices.

The 'end-to-end' and 'without external generators' wording is overstated: the system relies on a frozen pretrained Hunyuan3D VAE, and visual materials are produced by Hunyuan3D's separate material generator. The evaluation should clearly distinguish native geometry generation from the externally generated appearance used by CLIP-IQA, MUSIQ, CLIP, and human raters.

Originality is plausible but not yet established convincingly relative to prior MoT-based unified models and ShapeLLM-Omni. The main contribution appears to be a particular combination and specialization of pretrained Qwen3-VL and Hunyuan3D components; stronger controlled comparisons are needed to show that the proposed mode-binding principle itself provides the gains.

The impact statement is boilerplate. It does not address licenses and permissible use of aggregated 3D assets, participant consent or compensation for the user study, or foreseeable copyright and misuse issues for generated assets. These omissions are not necessarily prohibitive alone, but the ethical and data-governance treatment is inadequate.

strengths: [Originality/significance] The paper tackles a useful problem: bringing detailed 3D generation and captioning into a unified vision-language model. Binding separate transformers to sequential token modeling and parallel block modeling is a plausible extension of mixture-of-transformer designs.

[Soundness] The reported results show a consistent advantage over the two evaluated MLLM-based generation baselines. On the stated test set, the method improves over ShapeLLM-Omni from 13.11 to 12.55 p-FID and from 0.29 to 0.27 p-KID, while producing substantially better image-based caption metrics than the Qwen3-VL-2B backbone.

[Analysis] The ablations provide some useful evidence that the Hunyuan3D-2.1 VAE, MoT architecture, larger backbone, and increased token budget each contribute to generation quality. The runtime and memory measurements also give an initial view of scaling behavior.

[Presentation] The high-level architecture is understandable, and the manuscript includes extensive qualitative examples, comparisons with both MLLM and conventional 3D generators, and visible failure cases.

[Limitations] The authors appropriately acknowledge ambiguous-input failures, hallucinations, information loss caused by watertight preprocessing, the restricted 3D-caption data, and the remaining quality gap to leading non-MLLM systems.
weaknesses: [Soundness—decisive] The claimed transfer from 3D generation to perception is not established. The paper compares the jointly trained model with the original Qwen3-VL, but changes training data, architecture, and objectives simultaneously. It needs a controlled captioning ablation with and without the 3D-generation objective; the current comparison cannot attribute the improvement to generation.

[Soundness—decisive] The central end-to-end claim is overstated. Section 3.3 applies Hunyuan3D-2.1's separate material generator after geometry decoding, while the conclusion claims generation 'without relying on external generators.' The evaluation and qualitative displays do not isolate what quality comes from CG-MLLM versus this external material stage.

[Evaluation] The quantitative protocol is seriously under-specified: the test-set size, render views and settings, feature extraction for p-FID/p-KID, conditioning protocol, baseline checkpoints and inference settings, and treatment of failed samples are omitted. Small gains such as 12.55 versus 13.11 p-FID are reported without seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

[Evaluation] Evidence is narrow relative to the claims. Generation is evaluated on one object subset, text-to-3D receives no quantitative evaluation, and there are no topology, geometric-detail, multi-view consistency, or prompt-compositionality measures. The method remains behind several non-MLLM generators on important metrics, so claims of high-fidelity 3D generation and 'clear superiority' require qualification.

[Evaluation] The user study is not reproducible or interpretable. '100 questionnaires' and approximately 2,400 data points do not reveal the number or demographics of participants, rating scale, comparison interface, sampling and randomization procedure, aggregation method, uncertainty, compensation, consent, or ethics oversight.

[Method/reproducibility] Essential implementation details are absent, including the precise shared-attention computation and masks, block construction, positional indexing, connector architecture, trainable versus frozen modules, loss definitions and weights, parameter counts, training-step schedule, batch mixture, dataset sizes, caption/instruction construction, optimizer settings, seeds, and total compute. No code, model, or processed-data release is specified. Others could not reliably reproduce the result from this manuscript.

[Efficiency] The advertised threefold speedup over token-level processing is not documented by a matched baseline. Tables 4–5 only scale the proposed system, omit the inference hardware and comparison method, and alter sample composition across token lengths. They therefore do not substantiate the paper's strong lower-cost and efficiency claims.

[Originality] The system primarily combines Qwen3-VL, a frozen Hunyuan3D-2.1 VAE, rectified-flow training, and an existing MoT pattern. The mode-based transformer binding may be useful, but its distinction from prior integrated AR-diffusion/MoT systems is described conceptually rather than validated experimentally, making the methodological advance appear incremental.

[Presentation] Space is devoted to a generic rectified-flow tutorial while the novel mechanism remains vague. Several claims are imprecise or unsupported—for example, 'scaling-law trend' from a handful of configurations, 'physical consistency' without a physical evaluation, and captions that allegedly outperform ground truth based only on selected examples.

[Ethics] The generic impact statement does not address licensing or problematic content in large scraped 3D datasets, downstream misuse of generated assets, or the human-subject procedures for the user study. These omissions are material given the data sources and reported questionnaire experiment.

strengths: Originality/significance: Integrating a pretrained vision-language model with a continuous 3D VAE through specialized TokenAR and BlockAR transformers is a useful step toward unified language-image-3D modeling. Binding branches to serial versus parallel generation modes is a sensible architectural choice.

Soundness: On the toys4k evaluation, CG-MLLM improves substantially over the two compared MLLM-based generators. It achieves p-FID 12.55 versus 13.11 and 30.07, p-KID 0.27 versus 0.29 and 1.00, and the best reported visual-quality and user-preference results among those MLLM baselines.

The ablations provide useful evidence that the stronger VAE, MoT architecture, larger language backbone, and increased 3D-token budget each improve p-FID and p-KID. The reported inference scaling also suggests that 4096-token generation is practically feasible.

Presentation: The architecture and its multimodal interfaces are explained clearly at a high level. Main-paper and appendix visualizations show diverse, generally coherent objects from multiple viewpoints, supporting the qualitative fidelity claims.

The paper candidly reports failure cases, dependence on a lossy watertight preprocessing pipeline, limited token resolution, and the gap to leading non-MLLM systems. These are appropriate limitations and should not count against the work merely for being disclosed.
weaknesses: Soundness: The claim that learning 3D generation improves image-based 3D understanding is not established by the experiment. The paper compares the jointly trained model against off-the-shelf Qwen3-VL, but lacks the decisive controlled baseline trained on the same captioning data without the 3D-generation objective. Moreover, caption scores from image-input and 3D-latent-input models are not directly comparable.

The generation evaluation is underspecified: the manuscript does not state evaluation sample counts, rendering views/settings, feature extractor used for p-FID/p-KID, whether every baseline was rerun under identical inputs and preprocessing, or whether toys4k objects were explicitly removed from all training sources. Thus, the numerical differences—especially the small gap to ShapeLLM-Omni—are difficult to interpret reliably.

The user study lacks essential protocol details, including the rating scale, assignment of examples, participant recruitment, randomization/blinding, treatment of repeated judgments, uncertainty intervals, and significance tests. The statement that 100 questionnaires yielded about 2,400 data points is insufficient to validate preference differences such as 3.32 versus 3.28.

Several efficiency and quality claims exceed the presented evidence. The asserted threefold advantage over token-level autoregression has no matched timing baseline; Table 5 reports only CG-MLLM. Likewise, calling the output “high-resolution” is relative to prior MLLMs, while the authors acknowledge fewer than 4k latent tokens and quality below stronger non-MLLM systems.

Reproducibility is presently weak. Dataset sizes and mixture ratios, training steps/epochs, effective batch sizes, objective weights, detailed masking/routing definitions, optimizer schedule, model parameter counts, random seeds, and code/checkpoint availability are absent. The brief architectural figures and prose are not enough to reconstruct the system or its evaluation.

Originality is moderate rather than exceptional: the method primarily combines an existing MoT-style AR/diffusion design, Qwen3-VL, and a frozen Hunyuan3D VAE. A sharper technical comparison against closely related unified AR-diffusion models and controlled evidence for the claimed benefits of this particular specialization are needed.

Presentation contains some overstatement and ambiguity. “End-to-end” can be misread because generation relies on a pretrained frozen VAE and a subsequent material-synthesis component; caption references are short MLLM-generated descriptions, making claims that outputs outperform the ground truth problematic; and visual examples do not substitute for geometric metrics such as Chamfer distance, normal consistency, topology, or watertightness.

Ethics are treated only with a boilerplate impact statement. A generative 3D system warrants at least brief consideration of dataset licenses and attribution, memorization or near-duplication, copyrighted asset generation, and misuse. No major ethical violation is demonstrated, but the discussion is inadequate. Overall, the idea and results are promising, but evidential and reproducibility gaps currently outweigh the merits and require a substantial revision.
